reader.requirement: At --std 85 FUNCTION CHAR's argument value must lie in 1 .. the number of positions of the program collating sequence (native, or an ALPHABET with ALSO groups that collapse positions); every value in that range must return the character at that ordinal, and a value outside it leaves the result undefined (§1989:A.2.2), so no particular response is required for it.

reader.notes: The domain is the collation's PositionCount (65,536 native code units, fewer under ALSO), and CharAt is the exact inverse of Weight, so every in-range value returns its character. Out-of-range values return one space (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION when checking is on), inside the undefined result §1989:A.2.2 grants.

refuter.evidence: The reader probed the native sequence and an ALSO alphabet; I probed the two program collating sequences the reader did not. xchar1.cob (PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS S1, ALPHABET S1 IS STANDARD-1) at --std 85: S1-CHAR66=[A], S1-CHAR1=LOW YES, ORD (CHAR (97)) = 00097: every ordinal of the X3.4 sequence maps to its character; ORD (HIGH-VALUE) = 65536 and CHAR (128) is not HIGH-VALUE, i.e. the compiler extends the 128-position STANDARD-1 sequence with the remaining native characters, a correspondence §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4a leaves to the implementor (cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4a  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4a). xchar2.cob (ALPHABET A1 IS "Z" "Y" "A" THRU "C"): CHAR 1..5 = Z,Y,B at 4,C at 5, CHAR (89) = V, CHAR (90) = W, ORD ("X") = 91, exactly the literal positions then the unnamed native characters in native order. (MOVE FUNCTION ORD (...) TO N was correctly refused COBOL0900 at 85 and rewritten as COMPUTE.) cite.py: OK  §1989:A.2.9.3 AR2  (2.9.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR2; OK  §1989:A.2.2 (values outside the permissible range: result undefined). AR2 constrains the program's argument value; any value outside it is undefined, so no compiler response can violate it, and every in-range value probed returns the right character.
